editorial:
You're in for another wild ride with Gru, Lucy, and the girls as they juggle family life and villain-catching. This time, Gru discovers he has a long-lost twin brother named Dru who is desperate to pull him back into the bad-guy business. Meanwhile, former '80s child star Balthazar Bratt is plotting world domination with dance moves and shoulder pads. The whole thing is bright, silly, and packed with Minion chaos from start to finish.

The animation looks sharp and colorful, and Steve Carell is clearly having a blast voicing both Gru and Dru. The '80s soundtrack is a fun bonus, and the Minions deliver plenty of slapstick laughs. On the downside, the story jumps around a lot and some jokes feel recycled from earlier films. Still, it's a solid pick for family movie night. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or pick up the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Gru and Dru team up to stop Balthazar Bratt from stealing the world's biggest diamond and launching his giant robot into space. After a big dance-fight showdown, Bratt is defeated and arrested. Gru decides to stay a good guy but keeps his bond with Dru, who joins the Anti-Villain League. The Minions return to Gru's side, and the family celebrates together, hinting at more adventures ahead.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves animated family comedies with silly humor.
